llm.summary: The skill broadly matches its Douyin trend-report purpose, but it fetches data with TLS verification disabled and automatically creates report files, so users should review it before installing.

dimensions.detail: Fetching Douyin hot-list data, analyzing trends, offering subscriptions, and generating HTML/PDF reports are described in the skill and fit the stated creator-operations purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The workflow makes HTML and PDF generation mandatory after queries and forbids asking the user first, which creates local artifacts even for simple lookups.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No elevated installer, credential setup, or privileged install path is shown; generated HTML does load third-party CDN JavaScript for export features when opened.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Both Python scripts connect to a hard-coded IP for onetotenvip.com with certificate verification and hostname checking disabled, then use the returned data in generated HTML, which is disproportionate for a normal trend lookup tool.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes HTML/PDF report files automatically and describes recurring push preferences; subscription recording requires confirmation, but file creation is not user-directed.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a local Python skill contacting a third-party service, creating HTML/PDF reports automatically, and opening generated HTML that loads CDN JavaScript. Treat fetched links and report contents cautiously unless the network code is changed to use normal HTTPS verification and exported content is generated only after explicit user approval.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Network fetching and report creation are part of the advertised workflow, but the metadata does not clearly declare those capabilities or boundaries.
[SDI-1] expected: HTML report generation is advertised, but making it automatic and mandatory is broader than needed for every query.
[SDI-2] expected: PDF export is disclosed as a feature, but requiring it for all lookups creates unnecessary persistent output.
[SDI-4] expected: CDN libraries support the export UI, but the skill describes the HTML as standalone without clearly explaining runtime third-party script loading.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger phrases match the hot-trend domain, but they can activate the skill from ambiguous conversation despite side effects.
[SQP-2] expected: Automatic file creation is disclosed in the notes, but the workflow explicitly prevents asking for consent before writing report artifacts.
[SQP-2] expected: Subscription preferences are purpose-aligned and the artifacts say confirmation is required, so this is a lower concern than the automatic file generation.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Disabling TLS certificate and hostname verification while fetching third-party data is not necessary for the stated purpose and materially weakens trust in generated report contents.
